THE DAILY METALS PULSE | Friday, November 27  
Weekly Close  
#Uranium #Silver #Gold #Copper

🥈 Silver gave back $44. It still finished the week up 5.1%.

New York silver futures closed at $43.17 an ounce, up 7.8% on Friday after trading above $44 earlier in the day. Gold futures settled at $3,639.60, up 2.9% on the day and 3.5% for the week. Both metals rallied alongside equities even as the US 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 4.94% from 4.85% on Wednesday.

🏦 Stronger US growth leaves the Fed room to raise rates

The US revised third-quarter growth up from 3.4% to 4.3% annualized. October inflation, measured by the Fed’s preferred PCE index, came in at 3.8% year on year, or 3.3% excluding food and energy. Friday added another piece to the picture: the US goods trade deficit widened 10.7% to $149.5 billion as imports hit a record.

For gold, the question going into December is whether buyers will keep stepping in with Treasuries offering close to 5%. Friday showed they were willing to. Next week’s jobs report could test that conviction.

🏭 Copper rebounds ahead of China’s factory survey

US copper futures finished Friday up 3.4% at $5.52 a pound. China reported that industrial profits rose 20.1% year on year in October, but economists still expect Monday’s manufacturing PMI to come in at 49.4. That would mark a second month of contraction. I’ll be watching new orders for a sign that stronger profits are translating into busier factories.

⚛️ Uranium miners gained nearly 11% for the week

The Sprott Uranium Miners ETF closed Friday at $37.27, up 5.6% on the day. The S&P 500 also had a strong week, gaining 5.6%. Monday brings a separate read on the physical uranium market when Platts resumes its daily U₃O₈ assessment after Thanksgiving.

👀 Three dates for the week ahead

• Sunday, Nov 29 — OPEC+ meets after Brent settled at $95.44 a barrel, up 3.1% for the week. Keeping first-quarter output targets steady is the expected outcome. A surprise could move oil before metals trading gets underway.

• Monday, Nov 30 — China’s official manufacturing PMI gives copper traders the first chance to see whether November demand beat those subdued expectations.

• Friday, Dec 4 · 14:30 CET / 8:30 a.m. ET — US payrolls. A strong hiring number could push Treasury yields closer to 5%. A softer one could give gold and silver room to extend this week’s gains.

thread_tweets.text:
Once again, it all comes down to your time horizon.

If your time horizon is two weeks to three months, you’re trying to time the market. You may want to wait for the VIX term structure to return to contango.

If your time horizon is two years, when the VIX hits 40, the S&P 500 is down 10% and the Nasdaq is down 20%, you buy regardless of backwardation or contango.

But most importantly, you need to understand what’s driving the selloff. In this case, the market was questioning the AI investment thesis. I understood the concern, but I didn’t share it.

That’s very different from COVID, when I didn’t understand the event or its potential implications.

Understand the risk, think in probabilities and invest according to your time horizon.

If your time horizon is two weeks to three months, you’re trying to time the market. You may want to wait for the VIX term structure to return to contango.

If your time horizon is two years, when the VIX hits 40, the S&P 500 is down 10% and the Nasdaq is down 20%, you buy regardless of backwardation or contango.

But most importantly, you need to understand what’s driving the selloff. In this case, the market was questioning the AI investment thesis. I understood the concern, but I didn’t share it.

That’s very different from COVID, when I didn’t understand the event or its potential implications.

Understand the risk, think in probabilities and invest according to your time horizon.

tweets.full_text:
This is how I avoided the COVID crash in 2020.

The $VIX was in backwardation, and I didn’t understand what was happening in the world or its potential implications.

These are my two red flags when shorting volatility or getting out of the markets completely: $VIX backwardation and an event whose implications I don’t understand.

When I don’t understand the risk, I stay out.

The lessons I learned helped me avoid the COVID crash two years later. That’s the beauty of the markets. There’s no shame in admitting your past mistakes if you’ve learned from them and become a better investor.
The shame is in repeating them.

tweets.text:
There is this huge divergence between the intellectual beliefs equity PMs hold and what the market is showing. Intuitively I don't really know why people are listening to someone down 65% YTD and blew up his fund once. 

"But hes smart" - the common fallacy - intellect has little to no correlation with how much you make in markets. Personally I had to relearn this cycle because I myself believed too much in equity reports, remembering that "I had no edge in stocks". What ended up happening was just holding these stocks because "they have backlogs till 2028!"

This is something to remember - complexity sells, but simplicity is the truth.

Some of my thoughts on the trend of protocols launching on @Enter_Elysium rn, drawing parallels to what I observed on early days RH chain:

Phase 1: launchpad war / Meme era

Elys started off with mostly launchpad and memes (Ascend, Montra, Eaac, Eaccat, Blob etc) not much value buying here other than trying to potentially position for the winning pad + greatest mindshare meme

Phase 2: Cool tech bro

then follows the actual “cool tech” phase, where teams building here are focused on solving some unique problem in its own kind (this is where I think we are rn) and imo this is one of the easier phases to capitalize on; as it’s easier to sieve through the tech and problem statement each protocol is solving vs trying to see which meme has more social capital for i.e

Phase 3: Slop tech

As price of the cool tech protocols float up, the next wave that naturally follows will be “slop-tech”, where extractors come to find a home for easy capital to fomo and chase the cool tech betas. This is where you’ll find a slop version of a cool tech protocol built in 2 days but tweaked v1.1 to add some feature and spin it off as its own. 

Since slop tech founders dgaf about building long term, they can’t or won’t innovate past v1.1, unlike the cool tech protocols teams could, naturally value wouldn’t accrue there over time past the hype phase

Phase 4: Capital inflow slowdown

Capital inflow eventually slows down to Elys chain esp if everyone who wants to be allocated has allocated. Arrival of slop tech means that any one late to Elys would be chasing these beta plays over the incumbent in hope for larger gains. But because these slop tech founders aren’t here because they want to for the tech but mainly capital flows to feast on easy rotational capital, safe to assume that capital will be rolled off via Elys to their bank accounts 

Phase 5: Consolidation of capital

Large pullbacks across the entire eco happens as the last buyer has bought, and no net inflow is happening at current valuations. A general consolidation / pullback to where “fair value” exists for all projects and this means 70-80+% drawdowns. Slop tech goes to 0, cool tech continues to build and chart establishes a range. 

Eventually the consolidation reaches an apex and a fundamental trigger reignited the capital inflow back into the chain and we go back to phase 2, where capital first reallocated to the cool tech and the cycle repeats

I think we are in phase 2 rn for Elysium

I am about 30 pages into the Q3 Situational Awareness letter. The full letter is 160 pages.

All I can say so far is that if Leopold is right about where he sees AI going...the disconnect between market valuations across the AI stack and the level of growth we should expect is one of the largest disconnects we have ever seen in financial markets.

Some of these predictions are quite hard to believe, but I guess that's also the point of his fund. He writes, "Either we or the market will have an extraordinary amount of egg on the face in a year."

Will post deeper thoughts tomorrow after reading through the whole thing, the most interesting insights so far: he thinks the frontier labs will do $1T of ARR by end of 2027, a ChatGPT moment for Robotics will come by late 2027, and that RSI is significantly being discounted by the market which could end up becoming so strong that it could lead to the shutdown of all models by the government.

We are living in one of the craziest times to be an investor.
